title: Leaves for healing (Revelation 22:1–5)
hook: a river of life, and a tree whose leaves heal the nations

segments.voice: Yesterday, the city with open gates: twelve pearls, no temple, no night. Your line was the gates are never shut. Who did you leave a door open for? Day one thousand three hundred fourteen.

The Bible's first garden has a tree of life in the middle of it. The last time Genesis shows that tree, there's a guard in front of it. After the man and woman are sent out, the King James says God placed "Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life." The garden is left behind, and the story moves on. Now turn to the last chapter of the Bible. An angel shows John a river, clear as crystal, running out from the throne down the middle of the city's street. And on either side of the river stands the tree of life. No cherubim. No sword. And its leaves have a job.

First, the river: "a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb." The prophet Ezekiel once saw a river flowing out from the temple, getting deeper as it went, with trees on its banks whose fruit was for food and whose leaf was for medicine. Revelation takes up that picture and sets it in the holy city. Second, the tree, which "bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month." Never out of season. There's no month when the branches are bare. Third, the leaves: "and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations." Not one people. The nations. Earlier in this same book, the text says "the nations were angry." Here they're being healed. And healing means there were wounds. Readers have asked why a city with no more pain still needs leaves for healing. Some hear healing that has already done its work. Others hear the long mending of old wounds between peoples, still going on in the light of the city. The text doesn't settle it, and it doesn't have to. Fourth, what's gone and what's given. "And there shall be no more curse." Some readers hear the curse that followed the first garden lifted here. Then a line to set beside the story of Moses, who was told that no one could see God's face and live: "And they shall see his face." The way to the tree is open again, and the face is no longer hidden.
screen: `NO MORE CURSE. THEY SEE HIS FACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: touch a leaf. A houseplant, a tree outside the door, a sprig of herbs in the kitchen, even a leaf in a picture if that's all there is. Hold it lightly between your fingers. Settle, and breathe. Notice its veins, its edges, how thin it is, and how it keeps a whole plant alive by taking in light. Then think of one wound between people you know: two relatives, two neighbors, two sides of a group chat. Don't fix it. Just hold the leaf and hold them. If you pray, you can bring them by name. If you don't, just breathe with the leaf in your hand. The bell holds the time.
Leaves for healing. The tree of life by the river in Revelation twenty-two, bearing fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations.

Your line: the healing of the nations. Today, do one small healing thing between two people: a kind word passed along, a misunderstanding cleared up, a peace offered first. Day one thousand three hundred fourteen.

howItsDone: Some Christians read Revelation 22 alongside Genesis 2–3 as the Bible's last garden answering its first, and some churches read 'the healing of the nations' at services of prayer for peace.

notes: Ezekiel 47 paraphrased (river from the temple, deepening, trees whose fruit is food and whose leaf is medicine). Confirm.
Two readings of why the healed city still needs healing (healing already done; ongoing mending between peoples) are given unranked. Confirm.
Exodus 33:20 paraphrased as 'no one could see God's face and live'. Confirm.
'No more curse' is linked to the curse after the first garden (Genesis 3); a common reading, presented as the text's echo. Confirm.
howItsDone: reading Revelation 22 alongside Genesis 2–3 is attributed to some Christians. Use at services of prayer for peace is described as 'some churches'; confirm.
Original: θεραπεία (Revelation 22:2 has εἰς θεραπείαν τῶν ἐθνῶν). The English 'therapy' link was deliberately left out.
Editor: the Genesis-curse link is now attributed to 'some readers', and 'a line that would have startled anyone' (a claim about listeners' reactions) became 'a line to set beside the story of Moses'.
Audit 2026-10-02: Genesis 3:24, Revelation 22:1-4, 11:18 and Ezekiel 47:12 checked; no change.
